# 041 — Static `/chains/<slug>` landing pages (014/021 pattern extended to chains)

## Goal
`specs/010-diagnosis.md`'s largest GSC failure class is "Crawled — currently
not indexed" (22,877 URLs), caused by 20k+ near-identical thin JS shells: one
`home.html` serves every parameterized URL, with real title/canonical/content
appearing only after client JS runs and a DefiLlama fetch completes. 014/021
fixed this for tokens end-to-end (`generate-token-pages.js` → real static
`/tokens/<slug>.html` → `sitemap-token-pages.xml` → sitemap index → CI-
generated on every `sitemap-update.yml` run). This item applies the identical,
already-proven mechanism to chains: 111 `sitemap-chain-*.xml` files still
point only at thin `?chain=<Chain>` shell URLs — the same unaddressed
category from the original diagnosis.

## Intuition
A crawler that can't run JavaScript (or times out before the DefiLlama fetch
resolves) sees every `?chain=Solana`/`?chain=Base`/etc. URL as the exact same
byte-identical homepage shell — indistinguishable duplicates, which is why
Google stops indexing them. The fix is the same one that worked for tokens:
serve a real, small, static HTML file per chain with server-delivered
title/description/content baked in at generation time, so there's something
genuinely different to crawl and index — no JS execution required. The page
still funnels interested visitors into the live, interactive `?chain=`
app view via a CTA; the static page's job is purely to be crawlable.

## What changed and why (diff in reading order)

**1. `generate-token-pages.js`** — one additive change: `escapeHtml` (already
defined, just not exported) is added to `module.exports`. No behavior change;
`test_token_pages.js` still passes 44/44 unchanged. This is the only edit to
the file that shipped 014/021/023/028-033/039/040, done specifically so the
new chain generator could reuse it instead of duplicating it.

**2. `generate-chain-pages.js`** (new file) — mirrors `generate-token-pages.js`'s
structure but keyed by `pool.chain` instead of token symbol, and **imports
rather than reimplements** the trust-rail gate and formatting helpers:
`isQualifyingPool`, `poolTotalApy`, `formatUsd`, `formatApy`, `escapeHtml`,
`renderAnalyticsBootstrap`, and every eligibility constant (`MIN_POOL_TVL`,
`APY_SANITY_LIMIT`, `MIN_QUALIFYING_POOLS`, `DEFAULT_LIMIT`, `SITE_URL`) come
straight from `generate-token-pages.js`. `chainSlug` is literally `tokenSlug`
under a local alias — it's a generic string slugifier, not token-specific.
- `rankTopChains`: aggregates qualifying pools (same `$100K` floor, same
  anomaly exclusion) by chain, tracks distinct token symbols per chain for
  the intro/description, applies the same 030/032/033-style "displayed
  top-8-by-TVL slice must include a visible non-zero APY" quality gate a
  chain-level thin/all-zero table would otherwise pass.
- `renderChainPage`: self-canonical `/chains/<slug>`, server-delivered
  title/description, `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD (Home → Chains (unlinked) →
  `<Chain>`), a written per-chain intro from real aggregate data (content
  genuinely different from the `?chain=` app view, not a re-render of it),
  a Token/Protocol/APY/TVL table (a Token column, unlike token pages, since
  one chain page spans many tokens), each row deep-linking to its
  pool-detail page, a CTA into `?chain=<Chain>`, and a related-chains nav
  (co-token chains first).
- `renderChainSitemap`: urlset of every generated `/chains/<slug>` URL.

**3. `generate-sitemap.js`** — a new `existsSync('sitemap-chain-pages.xml')`
guard block in the index-assembly step, placed immediately after the
pre-existing, already-shipped `sitemap-token-pages.xml` guard it mirrors
structurally line for line.

**4. `.github/workflows/sitemap-update.yml`** — a new "Generate chain landing
pages" step (`node generate-chain-pages.js --out chains --sitemap
sitemap-chain-pages.xml`) inserted before the "Generate sitemap" step, so the
sitemap index picks up the new chain sitemap in the same CI run; `chains` and
`sitemap-chain-pages.xml` added to the final commit's `git add` list;
`generate-chain-pages.js` added to the `push.paths` trigger list.

**5. `package.json`** — `"chains": "node generate-chain-pages.js"` script
(mirrors `"tokens"`); `test_chain_pages.js` added to the `test` chain, right
after `test_token_pages.js`.

**6. `test_chain_pages.js`** (new, 39 assertions) + `test_fixtures/pools-chain-sample.json`
(new fixture, fictional chain names `Big/Mid/Anom/Dust/Zero/Tiny/Trunc/Multi
Chain` mirroring the token fixture's naming) — exercises every gate branch
independently: floor exclusion, anomaly exclusion (content/count/TVL), the
0%-rounding gate, the top-8-truncation gate, slug safety (space→dash),
self-canonical/title/description, `BreadcrumbList` shape + XSS-safety,
CTA/pool-row links + fallback, related-chains ordering, and the analytics
bootstrap.

**7. `chains/*.html` + `sitemap-chain-pages.xml`** — 4 sample pages generated
offline from the new fixture, committed for review (mirrors 014's original
phase-1 practice). These will be overwritten by the next live CI run once it
generates the real chain set from `yields.llama.fi`.

## Deviations from spec (judgment calls)
1. **Shipped as one PR, not a phase-1/phase-2 split** — 014/021 split
   because phase 1's static-page mechanism was unproven; 021 already proved
   the full CI/sitemap-wiring pattern end-to-end for tokens, so there was no
   remaining exploratory risk to de-risk by splitting this item the same way.
2. **Trust-rail constants are imported, not restated** — the spec described
   "same `$100K` floor" as a property; the implementation imports the actual
   constant, a stronger guarantee (one source of truth, can't drift) than
   the spec's literal wording implied.
3. **`POOLS_PER_PAGE` stayed a local, independently-tunable constant** in
   each generator file (same value, `8`) rather than a third shared import —
   it's a display-density concern, not a trust rail, so no shared source of
   truth was needed.

## Verification
Verifier subagent: **PASS**, risk tier **HIGH** (independently assigned,
agreeing with the builder's guess — `.github/workflows/sitemap-update.yml`
is itself a NORTH_STAR-listed HIGH-risk config path, and this wires a new
generated-SEO-surface entry point into the sitemap index). 16/16 acceptance
criteria independently re-derived as met, zero failures. Full reasoning in
the verifier's report; build notes in `specs/041-notes.md`.

Environment limits (same wall every prior SEO-generator item hit):
`yields.llama.fi` is unreachable in this sandbox, so real chain pages only
exist after the next `sitemap-update.yml` CI run (same residual 021
documented). `node_modules`/playwright are entirely absent here — `test_smoke.js`/
`test_search.js` fail with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, confirmed pre-existing and
unrelated to this diff (neither file appears in the diff). Every other test
in the chain ran individually and green, well under the 5-minute timebox.

## Quiz

1. Why does `generate-chain-pages.js` import `isQualifyingPool` from
   `generate-token-pages.js` instead of redefining its own `$100K` floor /
   anomaly check?
2. Why did this item ship the CI + sitemap-index wiring in the same PR as
   the generator, unlike 014/021's original two-PR phase split?
3. Why does the "Chains" breadcrumb item have no `item` URL?
4. Why is `chainSlug` just an alias for `tokenSlug` rather than a new,
   chain-specific slugging function?
5. Why couldn't the real `/chains/<slug>` pages be verified in this sandbox,
   and what was verified instead?
